commencements.subject: Extradition: cases where a person has been convicted
commencements.description: Changes extradition test for category 1 convicted persons to require a retrial or review amounting to retrial.

commencements.subject: Respect orders
commencements.description: Creates the respect order, enabling courts to make it against adults on the balance of probabilities.

commencements.subject: Youth injunctions, housing injunctions and consequential amendments
commencements.description: Restricts anti-social behaviour injunctions to 10- to 17-year-olds and provides for adult injunctions.

commencements.subject: Maximum period for certain directions, notices and orders
commencements.description: Extends maximum exclusion under a police direction from 48 to 72 hours and adds inspector review.

commencements.subject: Fixed penalty notices
commencements.description: Gives accredited persons new powers to issue fixed penalty notices for community protection notice failures.

commencements.subject: Closure of premises by registered social housing provider
commencements.description: Enables registered social housing providers to close premises they own or manage that are associated with nuisance and disorder.

commencements.subject: Reviews of responses to complaints about anti-social behaviour
commencements.description: Requires local policing body confirmation of anti-social behaviour review recommendations where a local policing body case review takes place.

commencements.description: Nothing in this Schedule affects any power of a constable conferred otherwise than by this Schedule.

commencements.description: This paragraph applies where— a constable has reasonable grounds to suspect that there is relevant evidence in a vehicle, and the vehicle is not a dwelling.

commencements.description: This paragraph applies where— a constable has reasonable grounds to suspect that there is relevant evidence in or on any vessel or aircraft, and the vessel or aircraft is not a dwelling.

commencements.subject: Applications for search warrants
commencements.description: A search warrant may be issued under paragraph 5 only on the application of— a constable, in England and Wales or Northern Ireland; a constable or a procurator fiscal, in Scotland.

commencements.subject: Execution of search warrants
commencements.description: A search warrant may be executed by any constable.

commencements.description: This paragraph applies where a constable is exercising a power of search conferred by this Schedule in relation to any premises.

commencements.subject: Power to require production of documents etc
commencements.description: This paragraph applies where a constable is exercising a power of search conferred by this Schedule in relation to any premises.

commencements.description: A constable may use reasonable force, if necessary, for the purpose of exercising a power conferred by this Schedule.

commencements.subject: Obstruction etc
commencements.description: A person commits an offence if, without reasonable excuse, the person intentionally obstructs a constable in the performance of a function conferred by this Schedule.

commencements.subject: Introduction
commencements.description: This Part of this Schedule applies to applications in England and Wales or Northern Ireland for search warrants under paragraph 5.

commencements.description: A person applying for a search warrant must— state that the application is for a warrant under paragraph 5, specify the matters set out in sub-paragraph (2) or (3) (as the case may be), state what are the grounds for…

commencements.subject: Warrant: whether authorises one or multiple entries
commencements.description: A search warrant authorises entry on one occasion only, unless it specifies that it authorises multiple entries.

commencements.subject: Form of warrants
commencements.description: A search warrant must— specify the name of the person who applies for it, specify the date on which it is issued, state that the warrant is issued under paragraph 5 of this Schedule, specify each set of premises to be…

commencements.subject: Copies of warrants
commencements.description: Two copies must be made of a search warrant that specifies only one set of premises and does not authorise multiple entries.

commencements.subject: Introduction
commencements.description: This Part of this Schedule applies to the execution in England and Wales or Northern Ireland of a search warrant under paragraph 5.

commencements.subject: Warrant to be executed within one month
commencements.description: Entry and search under a search warrant must be within one month from the date of its issue.

commencements.subject: All-premises warrants
commencements.description: In the case of an all-premises warrant, premises that are not specified in the warrant may be entered and searched only if a senior officer has authorised them to be entered.

commencements.subject: Search of premises more than once
commencements.description: Premises may be entered or searched for the second or any subsequent time under a search warrant authorising multiple entries only if a senior officer has authorised that entry to the premises.

commencements.subject: Time of search
commencements.description: Entry and search under a search warrant must be at a reasonable hour unless it appears to the constable executing it that the purpose of a search may be frustrated on an entry at a reasonable hour.

commencements.subject: Evidence of authority etc
commencements.description: Where the occupier of premises to be entered and searched under a search warrant is present at the time when a constable seeks to execute the warrant, the following requirements must be satisfied— the occupier must be…

commencements.subject: Extent of search
commencements.description: A search under a search warrant may only be a search to the extent required for the purpose for which the warrant was issued.

commencements.subject: Securing premises after entry
commencements.description: A constable who enters premises under a search warrant must take reasonable steps to ensure that when the constable leaves the premises they are as secure as they were before the entry.

commencements.subject: Return and retention of warrant

commencements.subject: Increase in time limits for making claims
commencements.description: Increases time limits for making employment tribunal claims from three months to six months.

commencements.subject: Safety Representatives and Safety Committees Regulations 1977
commencements.description: Raises the time-off entitlement for safety representatives from three to six.

commencements.subject: Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992
commencements.description: Raises four periods in trade union law from three to six.

commencements.subject: Pension Schemes Act 1993
commencements.description: Extends the unpaid pension contributions period from three to six.

commencements.subject: Employment Rights Act 1996
commencements.description: Changes 'three' to 'six' in the time limits for written statements, wage protection, and tips information.

commencements.subject: Health and Safety (Consultation with Employees) Regulations 1996
commencements.description: Increases time off for representatives of employee safety from three to six.

commencements.subject: Working Time Regulations 1998
commencements.description: In regulation 30 of the Working Time Regulations 1998 ( S.I. 1998/1833 ) (rights as to working time), in paragraph (2)— in sub-paragraph (a), for the words from “three months” to “six months)” substitute “six months”…

commencements.subject: National Minimum Wage Act 1998
commencements.description: Extends the time limits for National Minimum Wage record access from three to six.

commencements.subject: Employment Relations Act 1999
commencements.description: In section 11 of the Employment Relations Act 1999 (right to be accompanied), in subsection (2)— in paragraph (a), for “three” substitute “six”; in paragraph (b), for “three” substitute “six”.

commencements.subject: Transnational Information and Consultation of Employees Regulations 1999
commencements.description: Routes European Works Council members' time-off complaints to employment tribunals in Great Britain; extends the limit from three to six.

commencements.subject: Merchant Shipping (Working Time: Inland Waterways) Regulations 2003
commencements.description: Raises two inland waterways working time limits from three to six.

commencements.subject: Civil Aviation (Working Time) Regulations 2004
commencements.description: Raises the civil aviation working-time rights limit from 'three' to 'six'.

commencements.subject: Fishing Vessels (Working Time: Sea-fishermen) Regulations 2004
commencements.description: Increases two rest and leave entitlements for sea-fishermen from three to six.

commencements.subject: Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006
commencements.description: Extends employee liability information and consultation time limits from three to six.

commencements.subject: Occupational and Personal Pension Schemes (Consultation by Employers and Miscellaneous Amendment) Regulations 2006
commencements.description: Extends the time limit for pension consultation claims from three to six months.

commencements.subject: Cross-border Railway Services (Working Time) Regulations 2008
commencements.description: Extends two working time periods for cross-border railway workers from three to six.

commencements.subject: European Public Limited-Liability Company (Employee Involvement) (Great Britain) Regulations 2009
commencements.description: Increases time off for special negotiating body members from three to six.

commencements.subject: Agency Workers Regulations 2010
commencements.description: Extends the period for agency workers' rights from three to six.

commencements.subject: Equality Act 2010
commencements.description: Extends the time limit for bringing discrimination claims at work from 3 months to 6 months.

commencements.subject: Merchant Shipping (Maritime Labour Convention) (Hours of Work) Regulations 2018
commencements.description: Extends seafarers' leave entitlement from three to six.

taxon_hygiene.title: Admiralty Court
taxon_hygiene.description: We handle shipping and maritime disputes. Cases that we hear include: collisions between ships disputes over the transport of cargo salvage of a ship, cargo or crew disputes over goods supplied to a ship disputes over mortgages and other security over ships claims by passengers for injuries suffered claims by ship crew for unpaid wages claims by shipowners to limit liability for loss or damage We handle both claims brought against the owner of a ship (‘in personam’ claims) and claims brought against the ship itself (‘in rem’ claims). We can also hear claims brought against other types of crafts (for example aircraft) as well as cargo. We can seize (‘arrest’) ships and cargos to prevent them being moved and can also sell them within England and Wales. Who we are We are a specialist court, part of the Business and Property Courts of the High Court of Justice. We are based in the Rolls Building, London. Cases are heard by one Admiralty judge, whilst other matters may be heard by the Admiralty registrar. Arrests, release and the sale of ships are handled by the Admiralty marshal. taxon_hygiene.title: The Business List
taxon_hygiene.description: The Business List contains three separate sub-lists: business financial services regulatory and pensions business. Business We deal with a wide range business disputes, often with an international dimension. Frequently these concern a business structure (company, LLP, LP, partnership etc) including: claims against directors for breach of fiduciary duty (the responsibility to take care of other people’s money) disputes about contractual arrangements between investors, such as share purchase agreements claims in tort, such as conspiracy or fraud, claims for professional negligence (e.g. against solicitors, accountants, surveyors, valuers) claims for breach of contract, specific performance, rectification and injunctive relief as well as other equitable remedies. Financial Services and Regulatory: financial claims where the Financial Conduct Authority is a party claims under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 claims involving regulators (other than the Pensions Regulator) Pensions Covers all claims where pensions are the subject matter of the dispute. Who we are We are a specialist court within the Business and Property Courts of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Rolls Building in London, as well as in the five regional Business and Property Courts centres. taxon_hygiene.title: Colin Kennedy
taxon_hygiene.description: Colin Kennedy is Chief Executive of The Mary Peters Trust, a leading Northern Ireland Sporting Charity. He started his career with the Halifax Building Society and rose to the level of Group Manager Northern Ireland before becoming Chief Financial Officer of one of Irelands largest Healthcare Companies. After selling this Company, he worked as a Consultant with various Organisations and Companies within the Private, Public and Voluntary Sectors including: Northern Ireland Voluntary Trust, The Community Foundation for Northern Ireland, The Millennium Awards Scheme, Belfast Women’s Training Services, The Ulster Sport and Recreation Trust and the General Dental Council. He is currently a member of the Nursing and Midwifery Council Fitness to Practice Panel, a member of the Mental Health Review Tribunal for Northern Ireland, a Commissioner on the Parades Commission for Northern Ireland and a member of the King George VI Youth Council in Northern Ireland. Colin has an MSc (Executive Leadership) from University of Ulster and is married with one son, living in County Down, Northern Ireland. items.legislation_title: Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026

commencements.subject: Tobacco vending machines
commencements.description: Creates an England and Wales offence for managers or controllers of premises where tobacco vending machines are available for use.

commencements.subject: Sale of unpackaged cigarettes
commencements.description: Makes it an offence in England and Wales for tobacco retailers to sell cigarettes not in their original packaging.

commencements.subject: Ban on manufacture of snus etc
commencements.description: Creates an offence of manufacturing snus or similar oral tobacco products in England and Wales.

commencements.subject: Ban on sales of snus etc
commencements.description: Bans selling, offering or exposing for sale snus and other relevant oral tobacco products in England and Wales.

commencements.subject: Possession of snus etc with intent to supply
commencements.description: Creates an offence of possessing relevant oral tobacco products, including snus, with intent to supply in the course of business.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Sale of vaping or nicotine products to under 18s
commencements.description: Creates an offence for selling vaping or nicotine products to under-18s, with a defence for age checks.

commencements.subject: Purchase of vaping or nicotine products on behalf of under 18s
commencements.description: Bans adults from buying or attempting to buy vaping or nicotine products for under-18s and adds a no-reason-to-suspect defence.

commencements.subject: Vaping and nicotine product vending machines
commencements.description: Bans making vape and nicotine vending machines available on premises, except in mental health hospitals.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Displays of products or prices in England
commencements.description: Creates a regulation-making power to restrict retailers' displays of relevant products and empty packaging in England.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Displays of products or prices in Wales
commencements.description: Gives Welsh Ministers power to regulate retailer displays of relevant products and empty packaging in Wales.

commencements.subject: Free distribution and discount of products
commencements.description: Criminalises public giveaways of products or coupons and substantial discounts to promote a relevant product in England and Wales.

commencements.subject: Restricted premises orders
commencements.description: Creates a right for the person who brought proceedings to apply for a restricted premises order against a persistent offender.

commencements.subject: Restricted premises orders: interested persons
commencements.description: Adds notice duties for applicants and representation rights for interested persons in restricted premises orders.

commencements.subject: Restricted premises orders: appeals
commencements.description: Allows appeals against restricted premises orders to be brought to the Crown Court.

commencements.subject: Breach of restricted premises orders
commencements.description: Makes it an offence to sell in breach of a restricted premises order, with a reasonable steps defence.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Power to extend restricted premises orders in Wales
commencements.description: Grants Welsh Ministers power to extend restricted premises orders in Wales by regulations.

commencements.subject: Restricted sale orders
commencements.description: Allows those who brought proceedings to seek court orders banning persistent offenders from selling tobacco, herbal smoking and cigarette products.

commencements.subject: Restricted sale orders: appeals
commencements.description: Grants a right of appeal against restricted sale orders to the Crown Court.

commencements.subject: Breach of restricted sale orders
commencements.description: Creates an offence for breaching a restricted sale order, with a reasonable steps defence and a fine on summary conviction.

commencements.subject: Liability of others for certain offences committed by bodies
commencements.description: Makes relevant persons liable for offences committed by a body with their consent or connivance.

value_diff.affected_entity: free distribution and discount of products or coupons
value_diff.law_span: A person commits an offence if— a the person— i gives away a product or coupon to a member of the public or sells a product or coupon at a substantial discount
value_diff.page_span: From 29 October 2026, it will also be an offence to sell vaping or nicotine products or coupons for these products at a substantial discount. This offence applies if the purpose is or effect will be to promote any of these products. A substantial discount is a price reduction that significantly lowers the cost of a product compared with its standard selling price. Whether a discount is substantial can vary depending on the product and the type of promotion. Selling products or coupons at a substantial discount is being banned to stop businesses trying to find a way round the free distribution offence.

taxon_hygiene.description: This list covers a large amount of Chancery work which is separate from the Business List. It includes the following types of work: Property landlord and tenant residential landlord and tenant commercial trespass/squatters mortgages land registry land – including title, easements, restrictive covenants orders for sale to enforce charging orders Trusts of Land and Appointment of Trustees Act 1996 (TOLATA) Trusts variation of trusts removal of trustees claims against trustees for breach of trust issues of construction/rectification trustees/personal representatives seeking directions including Beddoe applications (a type of application made by trustees) disputes about trust property applications for prospective costs order (deciding costs issues in advance) charities applications for administration order (appointing a person to manage a company that is in financial difficulty) Probate inheritance disputes (known as contentious probate claims) rectification of wills (cases against the way a solicitor has prepared a will) substitution or removal of personal representatives cases involving the Inheritance Act cases involving the Presumption of Death Act Cases are started in the Chancery Division. Who we are We are a specialist court within the Business and Property Courts of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Rolls Building in London. Cases in the Property, Trusts and Probate List are managed by the Chancery Masters and heard by the Chancery Division judges. taxon_hygiene.title: Administrative Court
taxon_hygiene.description: We review decisions made by people or bodies with a public law function, eg local authorities and regulatory bodies. We can: carry out a judicial review of decisions made by other courts, tribunals and public bodies hear challenges to decisions made by certain people or bodies (eg ministers or local government) where legislation has given the right to challenge We also hear: applications for ‘habeas corpus’, (a legal procedure where the court decides to rule on whether the detention of an individual is legal applications to prevent someone who continues to initiate groundless legal proceedings (a ‘vexatious litigant’) from continuing to do so without first obtaining permission from a court all applications under the Coroners Act 1988 (which deals with the appointment and conduct of coroners) appeals ‘by way of case stated’ from the Crown Court or magistrates’ courts (where our opinion is sought on a particular point of law where a mistake may have been made) applications for an order to imprison a person for contempt of court appeals under the Extradition Act 2003 (which deals with extradition requests to and from the United Kingdom and bail) appeals against decisions made by some professional bodies, eg the Nursing and Midwifery Council applications for ‘restraint orders’ or ‘certificates of inadequacy’ where assets have been frozen or confiscated We also contain a specialist Planning Court which handles judicial reviews of decisions about planning permission and other challenges to planning decisions. Who we are We are a specialist court within the King’s Bench Division of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Royal Courts of Justice, London and also at centres in Birmingham, Cardiff, Leeds and Manchester. Cases may be heard by one High Court judge or by a ‘Divisional Court’ which consists of 2 or more judges, normally a High Court Judge and a Lord Justice of Appeal. taxon_hygiene.title: Dr Ali Hashtroudi
taxon_hygiene.description: Dr Ali Hashtroudi, FFOM MSc LLM is a consultant occupational physician and Fellow of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine. He is the Clinical Director of Occupational Health and Safety Services, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust. He is the Medical Officer for South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service. He is an Honorary Senior Lecturer at Kings College London ( KCL ). He is the Head of the National School of Occupational Health at Health Education England. He is an Appointed Doctor under several legislations for Health and Safety Executive. He is a Health Examiner and Medical Supervisor for the GMC . His other appointments include membership of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Ethics Committee, Chair of the Higher Education Occupational Practitioners and Occupational Health Expert at the UK Advisory Panel for Healthcare Workers Infected with Bloodborne Viruses. He lectures for the Masters course in Organisational Psychiatry and Psychology at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neurosciences, KCL . His academic work includes publications in peer reviewed journals in the subject of occupational medicine and has presented nationally and internationally. He has authored a chapter in Fitness for Work a leading textbook in occupational medicine. He has a broad range of educational activities including clinical and education supervision of undergraduate students and specialty registrars in occupational medicine. He was previously the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Regional Specialty Advisor for South Thames region. In his current role as the Head of National School of Occupational Health he is responsible for the quality assurance of the training of the future occupational health practitioners. He served as a member of the Board of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine between 2007 and 2009, and on the NHS Health at Work Network Board since its inception in 2011 until 2017. He has a keen interest in the health of healthcare workers, emergency workers and students. He has a wide range of research interests including mental health and work, and biological hazards. He has supervised academic work of students from undergraduate level to PhD. He is a member of the Editorial Board of Egyptian Journal of Occupational Medicine.

findings.title: Administrative Court
findings.description: We review decisions made by people or bodies with a public law function, eg local authorities and regulatory bodies. We can: carry out a judicial review of decisions made by other courts, tribunals and public bodies hear challenges to decisions made by certain people or bodies (eg ministers or local government) where legislation has given the right to challenge We also hear: applications for ‘habeas corpus’, (a legal procedure where the court decides to rule on whether the detention of an individual is legal applications to prevent someone who continues to initiate groundless legal proceedings (a ‘vexatious litigant’) from continuing to do so without first obtaining permission from a court all applications under the Coroners Act 1988 (which deals with the appointment and conduct of coroners) appeals ‘by way of case stated’ from the Crown Court or magistrates’ courts (where our opinion is sought on a particular point of law where a mistake may have been made) applications for an order to imprison a person for contempt of court appeals under the Extradition Act 2003 (which deals with extradition requests to and from the United Kingdom and bail) appeals against decisions made by some professional bodies, eg the Nursing and Midwifery Council applications for ‘restraint orders’ or ‘certificates of inadequacy’ where assets have been frozen or confiscated We also contain a specialist Planning Court which handles judicial reviews of decisions about planning permission and other challenges to planning decisions. Who we are We are a specialist court within the King’s Bench Division of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Royal Courts of Justice, London and also at centres in Birmingham, Cardiff, Leeds and Manchester. Cases may be heard by one High Court judge or by a ‘Divisional Court’ which consists of 2 or more judges, normally a High Court Judge and a Lord Justice of Appeal. Court information Forms and guidance Judicial policies and practice directions Civil Procedure Rules , Part 54 Daily cause lists RCJ and Rolls Building daily court lists Case references used by the Royal Courts of Justice and Rolls Building User group meeting minutes Previous decisions Fees Extradition

findings.title: Admiralty Court
findings.description: We handle shipping and maritime disputes. Cases that we hear include: collisions between ships disputes over the transport of cargo salvage of a ship, cargo or crew disputes over goods supplied to a ship disputes over mortgages and other security over ships claims by passengers for injuries suffered claims by ship crew for unpaid wages claims by shipowners to limit liability for loss or damage We handle both claims brought against the owner of a ship (‘in personam’ claims) and claims brought against the ship itself (‘in rem’ claims). We can also hear claims brought against other types of crafts (for example aircraft) as well as cargo. We can seize (‘arrest’) ships and cargos to prevent them being moved and can also sell them within England and Wales. Who we are We are a specialist court, part of the Business and Property Courts of the High Court of Justice. We are based in the Rolls Building, London. Cases are heard by one Admiralty judge, whilst other matters may be heard by the Admiralty registrar. Arrests, release and the sale of ships are handled by the Admiralty marshal. findings.title: The Business List
findings.description: The Business List contains three separate sub-lists: business financial services regulatory and pensions business. Business We deal with a wide range business disputes, often with an international dimension. Frequently these concern a business structure (company, LLP, LP, partnership etc) including: claims against directors for breach of fiduciary duty (the responsibility to take care of other people’s money) disputes about contractual arrangements between investors, such as share purchase agreements claims in tort, such as conspiracy or fraud, claims for professional negligence (e.g. against solicitors, accountants, surveyors, valuers) claims for breach of contract, specific performance, rectification and injunctive relief as well as other equitable remedies. Financial Services and Regulatory: financial claims where the Financial Conduct Authority is a party claims under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 claims involving regulators (other than the Pensions Regulator) Pensions Covers all claims where pensions are the subject matter of the dispute. Who we are We are a specialist court within the Business and Property Courts of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Rolls Building in London, as well as in the five regional Business and Property Courts centres. findings.title: Dr Ali Hashtroudi
findings.description: Dr Ali Hashtroudi, FFOM MSc LLM is a consultant occupational physician and Fellow of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine. He is the Clinical Director of Occupational Health and Safety Services, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust. He is the Medical Officer for South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service. He is an Honorary Senior Lecturer at Kings College London ( KCL ). He is the Head of the National School of Occupational Health at Health Education England. He is an Appointed Doctor under several legislations for Health and Safety Executive. He is a Health Examiner and Medical Supervisor for the GMC . His other appointments include membership of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Ethics Committee, Chair of the Higher Education Occupational Practitioners and Occupational Health Expert at the UK Advisory Panel for Healthcare Workers Infected with Bloodborne Viruses. He lectures for the Masters course in Organisational Psychiatry and Psychology at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neurosciences, KCL . His academic work includes publications in peer reviewed journals in the subject of occupational medicine and has presented nationally and internationally. He has authored a chapter in Fitness for Work a leading textbook in occupational medicine. He has a broad range of educational activities including clinical and education supervision of undergraduate students and specialty registrars in occupational medicine. He was previously the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Regional Specialty Advisor for South Thames region. In his current role as the Head of National School of Occupational Health he is responsible for the quality assurance of the training of the future occupational health practitioners. He served as a member of the Board of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine between 2007 and 2009, and on the NHS Health at Work Network Board since its inception in 2011 until 2017. He has a keen interest in the health of healthcare workers, emergency workers and students. He has a wide range of research interests including mental health and work, and biological hazards. He has supervised academic work of students from undergraduate level to PhD. He is a member of the Editorial Board of Egyptian Journal of Occupational Medicine.

findings.title: Colin Kennedy
findings.description: Colin Kennedy is Chief Executive of The Mary Peters Trust, a leading Northern Ireland Sporting Charity. He started his career with the Halifax Building Society and rose to the level of Group Manager Northern Ireland before becoming Chief Financial Officer of one of Irelands largest Healthcare Companies. After selling this Company, he worked as a Consultant with various Organisations and Companies within the Private, Public and Voluntary Sectors including: Northern Ireland Voluntary Trust, The Community Foundation for Northern Ireland, The Millennium Awards Scheme, Belfast Women’s Training Services, The Ulster Sport and Recreation Trust and the General Dental Council. He is currently a member of the Nursing and Midwifery Council Fitness to Practice Panel, a member of the Mental Health Review Tribunal for Northern Ireland, a Commissioner on the Parades Commission for Northern Ireland and a member of the King George VI Youth Council in Northern Ireland. Colin has an MSc (Executive Leadership) from University of Ulster and is married with one son, living in County Down, Northern Ireland.
